relations.scope_of_equivalence: Only the explicitly selected source responses; no whole-item or whole-family equivalence inferred.
relations.differing_decision: Both obtain dy/dx by dividing parameter derivatives and use it to form a tangent at a particular parameter. Example22 supplies t=3; the exam first solves y=t(1+t)=0 to obtain two contact parameters and must return both tangents. That contact-point selection and repeated tangent output makes the selected textbook response easier. The general tangent in ii is source scaffolding, and elimination/sketch iv is excluded.
relations.best_member_reason: Among all six members, Example22(i)+(iii) alone explicitly ends in a tangent at a prescribed parameter, without a normal, area or locus response. Exercise4E Q4(i) only asks a general tangent; Q7(ii) does likewise; Q6/Q15 add less relevant general-parameter follow-ups.
relations.exam_task: Locate both x-axis contacts, then give each parametric tangent.
relations.independent_check: Exam t=0,-1; contact points (0,0),(20,0); slopes -1/18,1/22; tangents y=-x/18 and y=(x-20)/22. Source t=3 gives x-3y+9=0.

relations.scope_of_equivalence: Only the explicitly selected source responses; no whole-item or whole-family equivalence inferred.
relations.differing_decision: Both differentiate each parameter coordinate and form dy/dx. Q15(i) uses chain differentiation on cubic trigonometric coordinates and returns the general formula -tan t. The exam differentiates an exponential coordinate and the product 4t²e^(-t), then evaluates the quotient at the iterated parameter from (b) and rounds to 2 significant figures. The absent product-rule/exponential derivative and inherited numerical evaluation make the selected textbook subpart easier; its tangent/intercept follow-ups are excluded.
relations.best_member_reason: Q15(i) retains nontrivial composite-coordinate differentiation, unlike Example22 or Q7(i). Example23(i) has only elementary sine/cosine differentiation; Q6(i) is rational. No member asks the same numerical gradient at a previously iterated parameter.
relations.exam_task: Evaluate the parametric gradient using the preceding iterated t; give 2 significant figures.
relations.independent_check: Exam quotient: (8t-4t²)e^(-t)/(3+12e^(-2t)); source Q15(i) simplifies to -tan t.

relations.scope_of_equivalence: Only the explicitly selected source responses; no whole-item or whole-family equivalence inferred.
relations.differing_decision: Both use trigonometric parameter derivatives and dy/dx=(dy/dθ)/(dx/dθ). Example23(i) gives the general gradient -3cosθ/(4sinθ) for elementary trig coordinates. The exam has a sum containing cos2θ, so its x derivative needs a chain factor, and it requires the numerical value at θ=1 radian. Those extra derivative/evaluation demands make the selected textbook subpart easier. The normal, coordinate and sketch parts ii–v are excluded.
relations.best_member_reason: Example23(i) shares the sine/cosine parametric quotient most directly. Q15(i) uses cubic powers, creating a separate simplification demand, and still has no numerical evaluation. The four other members have polynomial/rational coordinates.
relations.exam_task: Differentiate the trigonometric parameter coordinates, then evaluate the gradient at θ=1 radian.
relations.independent_check: Exam gradient is -5sinθ/(3cosθ-8sin2θ), approximately 0.744018 at θ=1.

relations.differing_decision: The domain bullet explicitly asks for justification that y=log_a x exists only when x>0; explaining x=a^y>0 supplies the shared positive-argument principle. The exam applies it to ln(x-2) and requests the single numerical cutoff 2. The source requires an explanation of the basic graph, while the target adds an affine input shift and gives a numerical boundary, so this is a mixed structural branch of the named domain explanation, not same type or complete exam-style practice. The other four property explanations are excluded.
relations.best_member_reason: This family has one member. Its domain bullet is the matching requested response; comparing all five property explanations obscured that subpart. The How? wording explicitly requests justification, but this remains conceptual supporting practice for the numerical cutoff target.

relations.scope_of_equivalence: Only the explicitly selected source responses; no whole-item or whole-family equivalence inferred.
relations.differing_decision: Both differentiate an implicit product and isolate dy/dx. Q6(i) has the simpler affine product (x-6)(y+4)=2 and returns a general expression. The exam product 2e^(3x)y also needs exponential chain differentiation, includes y², and requires evaluation at (0,-5). Thus the named derivative subpart is an easier branch. The gradient calculation embedded in ii supports transfer, but the asked normal line is not silently treated as a gradient-only response; ii–iv are excluded.
relations.best_member_reason: This family has only Q6. Its separately asked i is the closest response; ii adds a normal line, iii a second intersection and iv asymptotes/sketch, so the entire chain is not the comparator.
relations.exam_task: Implicitly differentiate 2e^(3x)y+y²=15 and find the gradient at (0,-5).
relations.independent_check: Source dy/dx=-(y+4)/(x-6). Exam dy/dx=-6e^(3x)y/(2e^(3x)+2y), which gives -15/4 at (0,-5).

relations.scope_of_equivalence: Only the explicitly selected source responses; no whole-item or whole-family equivalence inferred.
relations.differing_decision: Both substitute a point into an already available implicit derivative to obtain its gradient. The exam must first recover the y-axis point by putting x=0 in the original curve, then gives only its gradient; Q6(ii) supplies (7,-2), then additionally takes the negative reciprocal and constructs the normal equation. Source normal-line construction and target axis-point recovery run in different directions, giving a mixed branch. The derivative in source i remains a dependency; source iii–iv and exam derivative proof (a) are not added to the selected outputs.
relations.best_member_reason: The sole member’s ii-normal contains the relevant point-gradient evaluation and then an explicitly retained normal-line demand. Source i alone omits the evaluation stage; the later second-intersection/asymptote/sketch tasks are further away.
relations.exam_task: Recover the y-axis crossing, then use the given earlier derivative for its gradient.
relations.independent_check: Exam x=0 gives y=2 and dy/dx=-4. Source at (7,-2) has tangent gradient -2, normal gradient 1/2 and normal y=x/2-11/2.

members.reading_note: Read all i–iv and the continuation solution/figure. Derives dy/dx=1/t, general tangent, tangent at t=3, eliminates t and sketches. Only i+iii are selected for BP-15; ii remains the source scaffolding dependency and iv is excluded.

Read all i–v and the continuation solution/figure. Trigonometric parametric dy/dx, general normal, normal at π/4, coordinates and sketch. Part i is the best family member for BP-37; normal/point/sketch outputs are excluded.

Read all i–iii. General tangent and normal for x=at²,y=2at, then normal-axis intersections. No prescribed numerical gradient or axis-crossing contact-point recovery; less close than selected Examples22/23.

Read all i–iv. Rational parametric gradient, general tangent, tangent-axis intercepts and invariant triangle area. No prescribed gradient evaluation; rational form is further from the trigonometric/exponential targets.

Read all i–iv and its given parabola sketch. Gradient=t, general tangent, intersection of tangents at two arbitrary parameters, then a straight-line locus. Later geometric algebra is not the target gradient or tangent-at-axis-crossings response.

Read all i–iii. x=a cos³t,y=a sin³t; part i requires chain differentiation of powers of trig functions before forming dy/dx. Later general tangent and constant intercept distance are excluded. Part i best preserves nontrivial differentiation for BP-24.

Read all five property bullets, graph and explicit How? prompt. The domain explanation alone is selected for BP-28/42. Intercept, asymptote/sign, growth and base-point explanations are excluded from those pair comparisons.

Read all i–iv. i derives the implicit derivative; ii asks the normal at the supplied point; iii asks the second intersection; iv asks asymptotes/sketch. Part i is selected for BP-31; ii-normal is selected for BP-43 with its extra normal-line response explicit.

prompt_policy_recommendation.status: Owner close-out integration policy confirmed by root; preserve accepted item-level tags.
prompt_policy_recommendation.selected_rule: Treat a specifically requested mathematical response as posed regardless of the Prompt label: a calculation, validity decision, domain or explanation is sufficient. Mere commentary or a rhetorical transition without an identified response is support-only. Conceptual prompts may still be supporting practice rather than same-type examination practice.
prompt_policy_recommendation.family_disposition_limit: A heterogeneous family lacking one common assessed demand does not make an individual member unposed. Keep member-specific assessed/support facets and do not create a new family or retag accepted item links merely to apply this policy.
